pages.quiz:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #18
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why is it a mistake to say there are four elements in the Panch Mahabhoot? (1 mark)
   A. There is only one
   B. There are five
   C. There are ten
   D. There are seven

2. Which is a good way to save water? (1 mark)
   A. Pour water on the road
   B. Close the tap fully after use
   C. Wash the car every day
   D. Leave taps running

3. Which element is called Vayu? (1 mark)
   A. Fire
   B. Earth
   C. Air
   D. Space

4. The soil in a shamba belongs to which element? (1 mark)
   A. Prithvi
   B. Akash
   C. Agni
   D. Vayu

5. Who was Prahlad? (1 mark)
   A. A river
   B. The young son of Hiranyakashipu who loved Vishnu
   C. A Sikh Guru
   D. A Jain monk

6. What does the story of the swan teach us? (1 mark)
   A. To be proud
   B. To hunt for fun
   C. To ignore suffering
   D. To be kind to animals and help the hurt

7. During which Jain festival is the Kalpasutra often read? (1 mark)
   A. Madaraka Day
   B. Paryushan
   C. Vasant Panchami
   D. Maha Shivratri

8. What does the essence of a scripture mean? (1 mark)
   A. Its price
   B. Its length
   C. Its most important message
   D. Its cover

9. Which is a mistake about scriptures? (1 mark)
   A. Keeping it clean
   B. Listening carefully
   C. Reading with respect
   D. Making fun of another faith's holy book

10. Whom did Ram marry in the Bal Kaand? (1 mark)
   A. Saraswati
   B. Sita
   C. Ganga
   D. Kaikeyi

11. What did Bharat place on the throne? (1 mark)
   A. Ram's sandals (paduka)
   B. A book
   C. A crown
   D. A lamp

12. What promise lesson do we learn from the Ayodhya Kaand? (1 mark)
   A. Keep your promises
   B. Forget promises
   C. Promises are for kings only
   D. Break promises

13. In Twameva Mata cha Pita Twameva, whom does the prayer speak to? (1 mark)
   A. A tree
   B. God
   C. A king
   D. A river

14. How should you receive prasad? (1 mark)
   A. With your right hand or both hands, and say thank you
   B. With your left hand only
   C. By snatching
   D. By refusing rudely

15. In which Kenyan towns are Mandirs found? (1 mark)
   A. None
   B. Only Lamu
   C. Only in villages
   D. Nairobi, Mombasa and Kisumu

16. What does dravinam mean in the prayer? (1 mark)
   A. Knowledge
   B. Wealth
   C. Mother
   D. Prayer

17. How did the boy in the example story practise Asteya? (1 mark)
   A. He found the owner of the purse
   B. He kept the money
   C. He sold the purse
   D. He hid the purse

18. Which is polite when alighting? (1 mark)
   A. Thank the driver or conductor
   B. Leave rubbish
   C. Push others
   D. Run into the road

19. You are sent to buy bread. What is honest behaviour? (1 mark)
   A. Say the bread was more expensive
   B. Buy sweets with the change
   C. Bring back the correct change
   D. Keep some change

20. Which is dishonest? (1 mark)
   A. Copying another person's work and calling it your own
   B. Returning a lost item
   C. Owning up to a mistake
   D. Doing your own homework

21. Which Jain teaching means not stealing? (1 mark)
   A. Ahimsa
   B. Satya
   C. Aparigraha
   D. Asteya

22. Which of these is honest saving? (1 mark)
   A. Taking from another's savings
   B. Hiding others' money
   C. Saving your own money and not taking from others
   D. Borrowing secretly

23. Amina pays Ksh 200 for sugar costing Ksh 150 and is given Ksh 100 change. How much extra did she get? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 100
   B. Ksh 50
   C. Ksh 200
   D. Ksh 150

24. What is Bhastrika called in English? (1 mark)
   A. The shining forehead breath
   B. The bellows breath
   C. The moon pose
   D. The hare pose

25. When should you practise yoga? (1 mark)
   A. While eating
   B. While running
   C. Right after a big meal
   D. When your stomach is not full

26. Which three things does yoga join? (1 mark)
   A. Water, soil and air
   B. Body, breath and mind
   C. Rivers, trees and fire
   D. Books, pens and paper

27. On which date is International Yoga Day? (1 mark)
   A. 12 December
   B. 21 June
   C. 1 June
   D. 25 December

28. Which is one of the four Purusharthas? (1 mark)
   A. Bhajan
   B. Aarti
   C. Moksha
   D. Namaste

29. What does Punarjanam mean? (1 mark)
   A. A festival
   B. A river
   C. A prayer
   D. Rebirth

30. Which principle is about kindness to all living beings? (1 mark)
   A. Prani Daya
   B. Purushartha
   C. Punarjanam
   D. Paramatma

31. What does Daya mean? (1 mark)
   A. Anger
   B. Kindness or compassion
   C. Wealth
   D. Speed

32. Which king protected a dove in a well-known story? (1 mark)
   A. Harishchandra
   B. Hiranyakashipu
   C. Ravan
   D. King Shibi

33. What does karma mean? (1 mark)
   A. Water
   B. Prayer
   C. Wealth
   D. Action

34. Which is a reason for celebrating festivals? (1 mark)
   A. To remember important events and teachings
   B. To waste time
   C. To stop learning
   D. To avoid friends

35. What is a rite or ritual? (1 mark)
   A. A river
   B. A school subject
   C. A special action done in a set way at a festival
   D. A kind of food

36. On which date did Kenya become fully independent? (1 mark)
   A. 1 June 1963
   B. 1 January 1964
   C. 21 June 2015
   D. 12 December 1963

37. Which day is linked with Saturn? (1 mark)
   A. Saturday
   B. Sunday
   C. Monday
   D. Thursday

38. Which day is linked with Mars? (1 mark)
   A. Saturday
   B. Thursday
   C. Friday
   D. Tuesday

39. Shukra is the Indian name for which planet? (1 mark)
   A. Venus
   B. Mars
   C. Saturn
   D. Mercury

40. Guru (Brihaspati) is the Indian name for which planet? (1 mark)
   A. Saturn
   B. Mars
   C. Venus
   D. Jupiter

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Why should we not pollute rivers? (2 marks)

42. Describe the story of Guru Nanak and Bhai Lalo and its lesson. (4 marks)

43. Write the Indian names for Tuesday and Wednesday. (2 marks)

44. Describe how to make a decorated calendar. (4 marks)

45. Explain the importance of celebrating Madaraka Day. (3 marks)

46. Give three reasons why prayer is a principle of Dharma. (3 marks)

47. Explain how a school can make festivals inclusive. (4 marks)

48. Give three ways of showing respect to any scripture. (3 marks)

49. Give two ways water is used at home. (2 marks)

50. State three rules of good behaviour when visiting a Mandir. (3 marks)

51. Give three benefits of yoga. (3 marks)

52. Explain how you would present a short skit on one Enlightened Being. (4 marks)

53. Describe how to do Sasankasana. (4 marks)

54. Give two safety rules for yoga. (2 marks)

55. Draw a timeline from January to December and mark Maha Shivratri, Madaraka Day and Paryushan. (4 marks)

56. Write three signs of integrity at school. (3 marks)

57. Name the months of the Indian traditional calendar in which Maha Shivratri and Paryushan fall. (3 marks)

58. Name two sacred rivers mentioned in the lesson. (2 marks)

59. State two things people do on Maha Shivratri. (2 marks)

60. Describe how the Bodhi tree is linked with the Buddha. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #18 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — There are five
   Panch means five.

2. B — Close the tap fully after use
   Closing taps stops waste.

3. C — Air
   Vayu means air and wind.

4. A — Prithvi
   Soil is earth, or Prithvi.

5. B — The young son of Hiranyakashipu who loved Vishnu
   Prahlad stayed faithful to Vishnu.

6. D — To be kind to animals and help the hurt
   Siddhartha showed kindness.

7. B — Paryushan
   Many Jains listen to it during Paryushan.

8. C — Its most important message
   The essence is the main lesson inside.

9. D — Making fun of another faith's holy book
   We should respect all scriptures.

10. B — Sita
   Ram married Sita in Mithila.

11. A — Ram's sandals (paduka)
   Bharat ruled in Ram's name.

12. A — Keep your promises
   Ram kept his father's promise.

13. B — God
   It speaks to God as parent and friend.

14. A — With your right hand or both hands, and say thank you
   Receive with politeness.

15. D — Nairobi, Mombasa and Kisumu
   Mandirs are found in many Kenyan towns.

16. B — Wealth
   Dravinam means wealth.

17. A — He found the owner of the purse
   He returned it.

18. A — Thank the driver or conductor
   Thanking shows good manners.

19. C — Bring back the correct change
   Bring back all correct change.

20. A — Copying another person's work and calling it your own
   Copying and claiming it is cheating.

21. D — Asteya
   Asteya is non-stealing.

22. C — Saving your own money and not taking from others
   Honest saving respects others.

23. B — Ksh 50
   Correct change is 50, so 100 minus 50 is 50 extra.

24. B — The bellows breath
   A bellows pumps air into a fire.

25. D — When your stomach is not full
   Do it with an empty stomach.

26. B — Body, breath and mind
   Yoga joins these three.

27. B — 21 June
   21 June.

28. C — Moksha
   The four are Dharma, Artha, Kama and Moksha.

29. D — Rebirth
   Punarjanam is being born again.

30. A — Prani Daya
   Prani Daya is compassion.

31. B — Kindness or compassion
   Daya is compassion.

32. D — King Shibi
   King Shibi saved the dove.

33. D — Action
   Karma is action and its results.

34. A — To remember important events and teachings
   Festivals help us remember.

35. C — A special action done in a set way at a festival
   Examples are lighting a lamp or raising a flag.

36. D — 12 December 1963
   Jamhuri Day is 12 December.

37. A — Saturday
   Shanivaar.

38. D — Tuesday
   Mangalvaar.

39. A — Venus
   Shukra is Venus.

40. D — Jupiter
   Guru is Jupiter.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Polluted rivers harm plants, animals and people who use the water, and take away the sacredness of the water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid reason.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Guru Nanak chose to eat at the home of Bhai Lalo, an honest carpenter, instead of Malik Bhago's feast. The lesson is that honest work is the best way to earn.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for Bhai Lalo, 1 mark for choosing his home, 1 mark for honest labour, 1 mark for the lesson.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Tuesday: Mangalvaar. Wednesday: Budhvaar.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Draw a table with seven columns, write English and Indian names, draw the Sun, Moon and planets above their days, and decorate it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: It reminds us of Kenya's step to self-government on 1 June 1963, teaches patriotism and unity, and lets us respect the flag and the anthem.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: It makes us thankful, calm and humble, gives courage, and reminds us we are not alone (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: Give clear instructions, help learners with special needs to take part, share food and clothes with the needy, and invite all faiths and communities.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Keep it clean, keep it in a high place, wash hands before touching it, listen quietly, follow its teachings (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: Drinking, cooking, washing, cleaning, watering plants or animals (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct use.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Remove shoes, dress modestly, speak softly, switch off phones, do not touch the murti, ask before taking photographs (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: It keeps the body flexible and strong, helps us breathe well and stay calm, helps us focus and teaches discipline (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

52. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a story, decide the characters, practise the lines, act it out, and then say what lesson it teaches.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for choosing the story, roles, practice, acting and lesson (any four).

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: Start in Vajra Asana, breathe in and raise the arms, breathe out and bend forward, rest the forehead on the mat with arms stretched forward, breathe calmly and come up slowly.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for four correct steps.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: Practise with a teacher, wear loose clothes, do it on a mat, do not do it after a big meal, stop if you feel dizzy (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: A line from January to December with Maha Shivratri in February or March, Madaraka Day on 1 June and Paryushan in August or September.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the line and months, 1 mark for each correct festival.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Not cheating, owning up to mistakes, handing in lost items, telling the truth, doing your own work (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: Maha Shivratri in Phalguna and Paryushan in Bhadrapada.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each and 1 mark for correct spelling.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: The Ganga and the Beas (or the Rijubalika).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct river.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: Fast, stay awake all night, bathe the Shiva Linga, offer bel leaves, chant Om Namah Shivaya (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

60. (3 marks)
   Answer: Prince Siddhartha sat under a Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya and became the Buddha, the Awakened One. Buddhists honour the tree because of this.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the tree, 1 mark for Siddhartha, 1 mark for enlightenment or Bodh Gaya.
